global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of loaves that must be baked. This tells the solver how many job entries (loaves) appear and that each must be assigned to exactly one oven.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical ovens available. The solver may place at most one loaf in each oven at any given time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List/collection of loaf identifiers (one per loaf). These are the job labels the schedule must cover; each identifier corresponds to one bake to schedule.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List/collection of oven identifiers. Use these identifiers when assigning loaves to ovens; ovens are identical but distinct for assignment and sequencing.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a single loaf (matches an entry from loaf_ids). Use this to refer to the loaf when assigning it to an oven and choosing its start time.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How long the loaf needs to bake (in minutes). If a loaf starts at time t on its oven, it finishes at t + bake_time_minutes and the oven is occupied during that interval.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest time (in the same time units) the loaf can be put into an oven. A loaf's scheduled start time must be greater than or equal to this value.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Target finish time for the loaf. Tardiness for a loaf is max(0, actual_finish_time - target_finish_time); the objective is to minimize the maximum tardiness across all loaves.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of print orders that must be scheduled onto the presses. Every order must be assigned to exactly one press and scheduled once; this integer determines how many job items to expect.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical printing presses available in the shop. Each press can run at most one order at a time; this is the capacity (parallel machines) for assigning orders.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers for the print orders to schedule. Each identifier corresponds to one job item with its processing time, ready time and due time.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for the individual presses (machines). Use these to record which press each order is assigned to; presses are identical so identifiers only distinguish resources.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of this print order, matching an entry from the print_order_ids list. Use to reference the order when assigning it to a press and a start time.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Amount of continuous processing time (time units) the press needs to complete this order once it starts. The job cannot be preempted and occupies its assigned press for this duration.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest time (time units) the order can start on a press due to preparation. The chosen start time must be greater than or equal to this ready_time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Target completion time for the order. If the order completes at time C, its tardiness is max(0, C - due_time). The objective is to minimize the maximum of these tardiness values over all orders.

global_fields.name: jobs

job_item_fields.name: processing_time

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Target completion time (minute) by which the scan should finish to be on time; tardiness for the scan = max(0, actual_completion_time - this deadline).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of order identifiers (each corresponds to one individual cut) that must be assigned and scheduled.

global_fields.name: machines

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest time (in minutes) when the wood for this order is prepared and the cut may start on a saw station.

job_item_fields.name: deadline

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical worktables available in the conservation studio; each table can process at most one task at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of task identifiers (IDs) for each restoration job; each ID corresponds to one item that must be assigned to a table and given a start time.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of table identifiers representing the available physical worktables; used to assign tasks to specific tables (machines).

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this restoration task; must match one entry in tasks_list and is used to reference its scheduling, assignment, and timing.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Amount of time the task needs on a table (in the same time units used throughout, e.g., hours or days). A task occupies its assigned table for this duration starting at its scheduled start time.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest time the task can begin because materials or preparatory work must be ready; the scheduled start time for this task must be greater than or equal to this value.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The promised completion time for the task. If the task's completion (start time + restoration_duration) exceeds this value, the overrun contributes to tardiness; the goal is to minimize the maximum such overrun across all tasks.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of client service calls that must be scheduled for the day (count of distinct calls/jobs).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical service vehicles (trucks) available to send technicians; each truck can handle one call at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the service calls (one id per call) used to reference each job when assigning to trucks and scheduling start times.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the service trucks (one id per vehicle) used to assign calls to specific trucks.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the specific service call; matches one entry from call_ids and is used to assign that call to a truck and a start time.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Expected on-site service duration for the call, given in minutes; once a call starts on a truck it occupies that truck for this many minutes.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest minute (relative to the scheduling day start) when the technician can begin the call because the client's window has opened; a call must not start before this time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Target finish time for the call, in minutes from the start of the scheduling period; used to compute tardiness as max(0, actual_completion_time - promised_finish_time_minutes).

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of setup tasks to schedule; each setup is a single task that must be assigned to exactly one lighting rig.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical lighting rigs available; each rig can run at most one setup at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the individual setup tasks that must be placed on rigs and given start times.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the available lighting rigs to which setups can be assigned.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of a specific setup task (must match one entry from the global setup_ids list).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Continuous time required to complete the setup on a rig (the rig is occupied for this duration once the setup starts).

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest possible start time for this setup because the required equipment or crew is not available before this time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Target finish time for the setup; finishing after this time contributes to tardiness, and the objective is to minimize the maximum such lateness across all setups.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of print orders to schedule. Each order must be assigned to exactly one printer and scheduled once; this is the count of all orders in the instance.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical printers available. Each printer can process at most one order at a time and is the resource to which orders are assigned.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the print orders. Use these IDs to reference each order's arrival, print duration, promised pickup, and assignment to a printer.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the printers. Use these IDs when assigning orders to specific printers in the schedule.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of a single print order (matches one entry from order_ids). This links the order's times and duration to its schedule assignment.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required for the printer to complete the order once it starts (a continuous or discrete duration). The scheduled processing interval for this order must be contiguous and have this length.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The time when the order becomes available for printing (earliest allowed start). The order's scheduled start on its assigned printer must be at or after this arrival_time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The promised pickup time for the order. If the order's completion time exceeds this promised_pickup_time, the positive difference contributes to that order's tardiness; the objective is to minimize the maximum of these tardiness values.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of compute tasks that must be scheduled across the fleet of servers; every task must be assigned to exactly one server and scheduled once.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical servers available to run tasks; each server can run at most one task at a time (no overlap on a server).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of unique identifiers for the compute tasks to be scheduled (each corresponds to one processing request that needs a start time and server assignment).

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of unique identifiers for the servers; used to assign tasks to specific servers when constructing a non-overlapping schedule.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of this compute task (must match one entry from the global task_ids list); used to refer to the task when assigning server and start time.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The amount of time the task needs on a server (processing duration); completion time = chosen start time + runtime. All scheduling decisions use this duration.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The earliest time the task can begin on any server (e.g., data arrival or task availability); scheduled start_time must satisfy start_time >= earliest_start.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The task's target finish time. Lateness for the task is max(0, actual_completion_time - target_completion_time); the objective is to minimize the maximum such lateness across all tasks.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of surgeries that must be scheduled and assigned to operating rooms; every surgery must appear exactly once in the plan.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of available operating rooms; each room can run at most one surgery at any time and surgeries are assigned to these rooms.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers for all surgeries to schedule; each identifier refers to one surgical case that needs a room and start time.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers for the operating rooms available for assignment.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for a single surgery (matches an entry in surgery_ids); used to refer to that case when assigning a room and start time.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The expected operating time for the surgery (in the instance time units, e.g., minutes); once started, the surgery occupies its assigned room for this duration.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The earliest time the surgery may start (e.g., when the patient and team are cleared and the room is ready); scheduling must not start the case before this time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The planned or target end time for the surgery; finish times after this are considered overruns, and the objective is to minimize the maximum such overrun across all surgeries.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of scenes that must be scheduled for shooting; each scene must be assigned to exactly one sound stage and given a start time.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical sound stages available; each stage can host at most one scene at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of scene identifiers (IDs) to be scheduled, e.g. scene labels used to reference each shoot.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of sound stage identifiers available for assignment (each represents one physical stage).

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a single scene (matches an entry from the scenes list); used to assign that scene to a stage and start time.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Planned duration of the scene's shoot (time it occupies a stage); used to compute the finish time from the chosen start time.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest possible start time for the scene because cast and crew must be ready by this time; the scene cannot start before this moment.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Time by which the scene should finish to be considered on time (the 'call time'); any finish after this incurs lateness measured as finish_time - call_time.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of meal batches that must be scheduled. Each batch must be assigned to exactly one kitchen station and given a start time.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical kitchen stations available. Each station can process at most one batch at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the meal batches to schedule; used to reference each batch's arrival, duration and deadline when building the plan.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the kitchen stations; used to assign each batch to a specific station.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this meal batch (matches an entry from batch_ids). Used to refer to this batch when assigning a station and start time.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Time in minutes required to prepare/cook this batch on a station. Once started, the assigned station is occupied for this duration.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest minute (from the start of the planning horizon) when the batch can begin because ingredients have arrived; the batch cannot start before this time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Target delivery minute for the batch. For a proposed schedule, lateness is max(0, completion_time - delivery_deadline_minute). The objective is to minimize the maximum of these latenesses across all batches.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of parcel processing jobs that must be scheduled (every parcel must be assigned to exactly one bay and processed once).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical sorting bays available in the yard; each bay can process at most one parcel at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the parcel jobs to schedule; each identifier refers to one parcel that needs processing.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the identical sorting bays where parcels can be processed.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the parcel job (must match one entry from parcel_ids); used to reference the parcel when assigning a bay and start time.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required to process this parcel in a bay (how long the bay will be occupied once processing starts).

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest time the parcel can start processing (the parcel's arrival to the yard); no schedule may start this parcel before this time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Target time by which the parcel should be completed for dispatch; tardiness for this parcel is max(0, completion_time - dispatch_deadline).

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of student presentations that must be scheduled; each presentation must be placed in exactly one classroom and given a start time.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of available classrooms; each classroom can host at most one presentation at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for the presentations to schedule (one identifier per presentation).

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for the classrooms available for scheduling (one identifier per classroom).

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the presentation (must match one entry from presentation_ids).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Length of the presentation (in the same time units used for release and deadline); the presentation occupies its assigned classroom for this duration starting at its chosen start time.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest time the presenters are ready to start their presentation; the scheduled start time must be no earlier than this.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The target finish time for the presentation; lateness for a presentation is max(0, actual_finish - allotted_finish_time) and the scheduling objective is to minimize the maximum such lateness across all presentations.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of vehicle services that must be scheduled across the lifts (an integer count of services to assign).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical car lifts available in the shop (each lift can process one service at a time).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each vehicle service to schedule (unique labels used to refer to each service entry).

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each lift in the shop (unique labels used to assign services to lifts).

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for this vehicle service (matches one entry from service_ids).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How long the service takes on a lift, measured in minutes. When a service starts, it occupies the assigned lift for this duration.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest time (in minutes since the shop opening / scheduling horizon start) when work on this vehicle can begin — the car's drop-off time; the service cannot start earlier than this.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The promised finish time for the service, in minutes since the scheduling horizon start. If the actual completion time (start + service_duration_minutes) is later, the difference is the service's tardiness.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of parts in the batch that must be scheduled; each part must be assigned to exactly one CNC machine and processed once.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical CNC machines available; each machine can process at most one part at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of part identifiers corresponding to the parts to be scheduled. Each identifier matches one job item entry.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the CNC machines available for assignment (used to map each part to exactly one machine).

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for the part (matches an entry in part_ids). Used to reference the part when assigning it to a machine and a start time.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Duration the CNC machine needs to process this part (in the same time units as ready times and due dates). Processing is non-preemptive and identical on any machine.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest time the part can start processing because material must be ready. A scheduled start time for this part must be >= this value.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Target completion time for the part. Lateness for a part is max(0, completion_time - due_date); the objective is to minimize the maximum of these latenesses across all parts.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of photo shoots that must be scheduled during the day. This is the count of distinct shoots the planner must place on sets and assign start times to.

global_fields.name: nr_machines

global_fields.name: jobs

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of identifiers for the available sets. Each identifier names a physical set where a shoot can be placed; used to assign shoots to specific sets so no set is double-booked.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for this specific shoot (must appear in the global shoot_ids list). Used to reference the shoot when assigning it to a set and a start time.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The duration of the shoot in minutes: how long the set will be occupied once the shoot starts. Start time + shoot_duration = actual wrap time for this shoot.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest possible start time for the shoot (in minutes from the schedule origin) because talent or required resources arrive. The shoot cannot begin before this time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The target wrap time (deadline) for the shoot in minutes. If the actual wrap (start + shoot_duration) is later than this, the amount late contributes to that shoot's tardiness; the objective is to minimize the maximum such delay across all shoots.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical backup units available; each unit can run at most one backup at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the backups to schedule. Each id refers to a single backup job that must be assigned to one unit and given a start time.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for the backup units (machines) onto which backups can be assigned.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of this backup (must match one entry from the global backup_ids).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Uninterruptible duration of the backup in minutes (how long the unit is occupied once the backup starts).

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest minute the backup can start because the source must be ready; start times must be >= this value.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Target finish minute for the backup. If the backup completes after this time, its lateness is completion_time - expected_finish_time (otherwise zero). The schedule should minimize the maximum such lateness across all backups.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical lab stations (workbenches or devices) available to run experiments. Each station can run at most one experiment at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the experiments to schedule. Each identifier corresponds to one experiment that needs a station and start time.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the available lab stations. Each identifier names a machine where experiments can be assigned.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a single experiment (must match one entry from experiment_ids). Used to link its timing and assignment data.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Amount of continuous time required to run the experiment on a station (its processing duration). Once started, the experiment occupies its assigned station for this duration.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest time the experiment may start — when its sample and preparations are ready. The scheduled start time must be no earlier than this time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Target finish time the experiment aims to meet. If the scheduled completion is later, the lateness contributes to the maximum tardiness objective (we ignore early completions).

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of setup tasks for the festival that must be assigned to crews and scheduled. Each of these tasks must be assigned to exactly one crew and given a start time.

global_fields.name: nr_machines

global_fields.name: jobs

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the crews (resources) that can be assigned tasks. Use these IDs when allocating each task to exactly one crew.

job_item_fields.name: job_id

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How long the crew needs to complete this setup once it starts (the task's processing time). Use this to determine the task's finish time given a chosen start time.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest time the task may begin because venue access or other constraints may block earlier starts. A task's scheduled start must be no earlier than this time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The planned finish time the task should meet. If the actual finish (start + setup_duration) is later, the positive difference is the task's delay; the objective is to minimize the largest such delay across all tasks.

global_fields.name: machines

job_item_fields.name: deadline

global_fields.scenario_description: List of session identifiers (IDs for each patient/session that needs scheduling).

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of nurse identifiers (IDs for each available nurse to whom sessions may be assigned).

job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a single vaccination session (unique ID for the patient/session).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time

global_fields.name: machines

job_item_fields.name: job_id

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How long the maintenance check takes once a team starts it (continuous processing time that must be reserved on the assigned team).

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest time the check can begin because required equipment/parts arrive on site; the assigned team cannot start this check before this time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Target completion time for the check; finishing after this time incurs tardiness. The objective is to minimize the maximum amount any check finishes past its target.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of mixing sessions that must be scheduled (each session must be assigned once to a room and a start time).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical mixing rooms available to host sessions (each room can run at most one session at a time).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the mixing sessions to schedule (each identifier refers to one session with its duration, earliest start, and desired wrap).

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the mixing rooms that sessions can be assigned to.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific mixing session (used to reference this session's duration, producer arrival constraint, and desired wrap time).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Required continuous time length of the session (how long the room is occupied once that session starts). Specify units consistently (e.g., minutes).

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest time the session may start because the producer must be on-site; the session start time must be >= this value (specify same time units as duration).

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Target wrap time for the session; finishing at or before this time is on time. Any later finish contributes to that session's lateness (finish_time - desired_wrap_time).

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of plated orders (dishes) that must be assigned to ovens and scheduled.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical ovens available in the kitchen to bake dishes.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each plated order (each dish) to be scheduled on an oven.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the ovens (machines) available for baking.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a single plated order (dish) — matches one entry from dish_ids.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Required baking time for the dish on an oven, expressed in minutes; the oven must be occupied for this duration once the dish starts.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest minute the dish can be placed in an oven (e.g., when preparation is finished); the dish cannot start baking before this time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Target minute by which the dish should finish baking to be served on time; tardiness for a dish is max(0, actual_finish - serve_time_minute).

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of subcontract tasks that must be scheduled (each task is assigned once to exactly one crew).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical crews available to perform tasks; each crew can work on at most one task at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for every subcontract task to schedule; these IDs are referenced by the task-specific fields.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the identical crews (resources) that tasks may be assigned to.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a single subcontract task (matches one entry from the global task_ids list).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Amount of continuous work time the crew needs to complete the task once it starts (same time units used throughout the instance).

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest time the task can begin because materials must be delivered first; the scheduled start must be at or after this time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Desired finish time for the task (contractual deadline). A task's tardiness is max(0, finish_time - contractual_deadline); the schedule aims to minimize the maximum tardiness over all tasks.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of photo shoots that must be scheduled across the studios. This is the count of distinct bookings to place.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical photography studios (rooms) available for booking. Each studio can host at most one shoot at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List (set) of shoot identifiers — the labels used to refer to each individual photo shoot in the instance and in the schedule.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List (set) of studio identifiers — the labels used to refer to each physical studio where shoots can be assigned.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for a single photo shoot (one element from the 'shoots' list). Used to reference this booking when assigning a studio and start time.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Duration of the photo session (how long the studio is occupied) for this shoot. Once started, the session occupies the assigned studio continuously for this length.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest possible start time for the shoot, representing when the client arrives and the session can begin; the scheduled start must be at or after this time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The promised finish (wrap) time for the shoot. If the scheduled finish exceeds this time the overrun contributes to tardiness; the objective is to minimize the maximum such overrun across all shoots.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of repair jobs (cars) that must be scheduled in the garage; used to indicate how many repair entries follow.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical service bays available in the garage where repairs can be performed.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of identifiers for each repair job (e.g., job numbers or internal repair IDs) used to reference jobs when assigning to bays and scheduling times.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each service bay (e.g., Bay1, Bay2) available for assignment.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this repair job that matches one entry in the global 'repair_ids' list; used to assign and reference this specific repair.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Continuous service time required to complete the repair, in minutes. Once the repair starts in a bay it occupies that bay for this duration.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest minute the repair can start (customer drop-off time), in minutes. The scheduled start for this repair must be no earlier than this time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Target completion minute by which this repair should be finished to be considered on time, in minutes. Tardiness for the repair is max(0, actual_completion_time - this value); the objective is to minimize the maximum tardiness across all repairs.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of aircraft turnarounds to schedule (each turnaround is a single service task that must be assigned to exactly one gate).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical gates available for servicing turnarounds; each gate can handle at most one turnaround at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of turnaround identifiers (one entry per aircraft service task to be scheduled).

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of gate identifiers (each represents an identical service resource where a turnaround can be performed).

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this turnaround (matches an entry in the global turnarounds list).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Established service duration for this turnaround: the time the assigned gate will be occupied once service starts.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest allowable start time for this turnaround, i.e., when the aircraft is ready for ground service; scheduled start must be at or after this time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Target completion time (on-time departure target) for this turnaround; any finish time later than this contributes tardiness = finish_time − target_completion_time, and the objective is to minimize the maximum such tardiness across all turnarounds.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of render jobs that must be scheduled; every listed render must be assigned to exactly one render node and given a start time.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical render nodes available for processing renders concurrently; each node can run at most one render at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of render job identifiers to be scheduled. Each identifier corresponds to a single render that cannot be skipped or duplicated.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for the available identical render nodes; used to assign each render to exactly one node.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this render job (matches an entry in the 'renders' list).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Expected running time of the render on a node (in the same time units used throughout). Used to compute finish times once a start time is chosen.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest time the render may start because its assets must be available; the scheduled start time must be no earlier than this.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Requested delivery time for the render. Any finish time after this contributes to tardiness; the objective is to minimize the maximum tardiness across all renders.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of individual artwork installations that must be scheduled and assigned to crews.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical installation crews available; each crew can handle one installation at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each installation (one per artwork) that must be assigned and scheduled.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the crews available to do installations.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this specific installation (matches an entry from installation_ids).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Expected time (duration) the crew needs on site to complete this installation once they start.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest time the installation can begin because the exhibit space must be free before work can start.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The scheduled exhibit opening time for this installation; finishing after this time contributes to tardiness.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of cars that must be scheduled for service this shift. Each car corresponds to one job and must be assigned exactly once to one bay.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of identical service bays available. Each bay can work on at most one car at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of identifiers for the cars to be scheduled (one identifier per car/job). Each identifier appears exactly once and refers to the corresponding service task.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of identifiers for the service bays. These identify which bay a car is assigned to when constructing the schedule.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the car (job) as given in the car_ids list. Used to reference this specific service task in assignments and timing.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The required service time for this car, in minutes. Once a car's service starts in a bay, it must run uninterrupted for this duration.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The earliest minute at which the car is available to begin service (its arrival time). The car cannot be started before this time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The promised completion minute the shop aimed to meet for this car. If the car finishes after this time, the positive difference is its tardiness; finishes on or before this time count as zero tardiness.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of concrete pours that must be scheduled; each pour is an indivisible task that must be assigned to exactly one mixer.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical concrete mixers available on site; each mixer can run at most one pour at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the pours (one identifier per pour) that need scheduling.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the mixers (one identifier per physical mixer) that can be assigned pours.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a single pour (matches one entry from 'pour_ids').

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Continuous duration required to complete this pour on a mixer (in the same time units used throughout); the pour cannot be split across mixers or interrupted.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest time the pour can start (the pour must not begin before this ready timestamp).

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Desired completion time for the pour; lateness for a pour is its actual finish time minus this deadline, and the schedule aims to minimize the maximum such lateness.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of incoming trailers that must be scheduled for unloading; each trailer is a job that must be assigned to exactly one dock bay.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical dock bays available for unloading; each bay can handle at most one trailer at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each trailer to be scheduled (one identifier per trailer/job).

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each dock bay (machine) that trailers can be assigned to.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the trailer (matches an entry from trailer_ids) for which the following attributes apply.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required to unload this trailer (its service duration). When scheduled on a bay, the trailer occupies that bay for this duration.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest time unloading may begin for this trailer (start of its arrival window); the schedule must not start unloading this trailer before this time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The promised time by which the trailer should be finished being unloaded; finishing after this time produces a delay (tardiness) used to compute maximum tardiness to minimize.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of rehearsals that must be scheduled (each rehearsal is a job that must be assigned once to a single room).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of identical rehearsal rooms available for scheduling rehearsals (each room can host at most one rehearsal at a time).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of identifiers for each rehearsal (these identify each group/session to be placed into a room and scheduled).

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of identifiers for the rehearsal rooms available (used when assigning rehearsals to specific rooms).

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of a single rehearsal from the rehearsal_ids list; used to reference that rehearsal's scheduling data.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The length of the rehearsal (processing time) in the schedule's time units (how long the room must be occupied once the rehearsal starts).

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The earliest time the rehearsal can begin (when the group is ready). A scheduled start must be no earlier than this time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The planned end time by which the rehearsal should finish to be considered on time; any actual finish after this time contributes to tardiness (finish_time - scheduled_end_time). The objective is to minimize the maximum such tardiness across all rehearsals.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of appointments (clients) that must be scheduled across the styling stations; every appointment must be assigned to exactly one station and scheduled once.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical styling stations available; each station can serve at most one client at a time and cannot split an appointment.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each appointment (one per client booking) to be assigned to a station with a start time.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each styling station where appointments can be placed.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific appointment (client booking) corresponding to one element of the appointment_ids list.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How long the stylist will serve that client (length of the appointment); the station must be occupied for this continuous duration once the appointment starts.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest time the client is available to begin service (client arrival); the appointment cannot start before this time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The intended end time for the appointment (the booked finish); tardiness for the appointment is max(0, actual_finish - scheduled_end_time) and the goal is to minimize the maximum of these across all appointments.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of prescription orders that must be prepared on the benches; each corresponds to one job that must be scheduled once.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical compounding benches available for preparing prescriptions; each bench can process at most one prescription at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the prescription orders to be prepared (one identifier per prescription/job).

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the compounding benches where prescriptions can be assigned.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the prescription/order; must match one entry from the global prescription_ids list.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Time in minutes required to prepare the prescription on a bench (continuous processing time once started).

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest time in minutes when the prescription's ingredients are available and preparation may start on any bench (cannot start earlier).

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Promised pickup time in minutes for the prescription; finishing after this time incurs positive tardiness (finish before or at this time gives zero tardiness).

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of package batches that must be labeled. A solver should use this to expect that many batch items must be scheduled and assigned to machines.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical labeling machines available at the hub. Each machine can process at most one batch at a time and every batch must be assigned to one of these machines.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the package batches to schedule. Each identifier corresponds to one batch entry with its processing time, release moment and due cutoff.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the labeling machines. Use these to assign each batch to exactly one machine when building the schedule.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the package batch (must match one entry from the global batch_ids). This links the batch to its processing time, release moment and due cutoff.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required to label this batch on a machine (processing length). When scheduled on a machine, the batch occupies that machine for this duration starting at its chosen start time.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest time this batch can start labeling (e.g., when it arrives). The scheduled start time for the batch must be no earlier than this moment.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Target completion time for the batch. Lateness for the batch is defined as its actual completion time minus this due cutoff; negative or zero means on time. The objective is to minimize the maximum such lateness across all batches.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of drone battery-swap sessions that must be scheduled (each swap is one job that must be assigned to exactly one charging pad).

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical charging pads available; each pad can process at most one swap at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the individual drone swaps to be scheduled (one entry per swap/job).

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the charging pads (machines) to which swaps can be assigned.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this specific drone swap (matches an entry in the global swaps list).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How long the battery-swap takes (in minutes); once started on a pad, the swap occupies that pad for this duration.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The earliest minute the drone is available for its swap (the swap cannot start before this arrival time).

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The expected ready time (due time) for the swap; if the swap finishes after this minute it is late by finish_time − expected_ready_time, and the schedule aims to minimize the maximum such lateness across all swaps.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of cakes that need decorating; the solver will schedule exactly this many cake jobs across the tables.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical worktables available for decorating; each table can handle at most one cake at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each cake job to be scheduled (one entry per cake). These IDs link to the cake-specific fields below.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each worktable. Jobs will be assigned to one of these table IDs.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a single cake job (matches an entry in cake_ids). Used to reference this cake's timing and assignment.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Uninterrupted time in minutes required to decorate this cake once started; when scheduled on a table it occupies that table for this duration.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest minute the cake is ready for decorating (cannot start before this time). The scheduled start time must be >= this value.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Promised delivery time in minutes. If the cake finishes after this minute, the tardiness equals finish_time - delivery_deadline_minutes; otherwise tardiness is zero. The objective is to minimize the maximum such tardiness across all cakes.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of sterilization cycles (items) that must be scheduled. Each cycle corresponds to one item that must be assigned to a sterilizer exactly once.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical sterilizers available at the station. Each sterilizer can run at most one cycle at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of identifiers for the sterilization cycles (the items) to schedule; each identifier refers to one cycle with its own duration, availability time, and target finish time.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the available sterilizers (machines) to which cycles may be assigned.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of this sterilization cycle (must match an entry in cycle_ids). Used to link the cycle's times and its assigned sterilizer and start time.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required to complete this cycle on a sterilizer. Once the cycle starts, the assigned sterilizer is occupied for this duration (no preemption).

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest time the item is ready for sterilization; the cycle's start time on any sterilizer must be at or after this time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Desired completion time for the cycle. A cycle finishing after this time incurs tardiness equal to (completion_time - target_finish_time); the scheduling objective is to minimize the maximum such tardiness across all cycles.

global_fields.name: nr_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of film screenings to schedule across the theaters; each screening must be assigned to exactly one theater.

global_fields.name: nr_machines
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of identical small theaters (rooms) available; each theater can show at most one screening at any time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the screenings (one entry per screening) referenced by the screening items below.

global_fields.name: machines
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the theaters (rooms) to which screenings can be assigned.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this screening (matches an entry in screening_ids); used to assign and reference the screening in the schedule.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How long the screening occupies a theater (runtime) measured in the same time units as other times; the theater is busy for this entire duration once the screening starts.

job_item_fields.name: release_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Earliest possible start time for the screening (e.g., when the screening and audience are ready); the screening's scheduled start must not be earlier than this time.

job_item_fields.name: deadline
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The slated end time for the screening used to judge timeliness; for a screening that actually finishes at time T_end the overrun (tardiness) is max(0, T_end − planned_end_time). The objective is to minimize the maximum such overrun across all screenings.
